chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Takbeer upon the deceased, so he said: 'Five. You should say in the first of them: I testify that there is no god but Allah, Alone, without partner. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.'

Then you should say: O Allah, this one enshrouded before us is Your servant and the son of Your servant, and You have taken his soul to Yourself, and he is in need of Your Mercy, and You are Self-Sufficient regarding his punishment. O Allah, we do not know from his exterior except goodness, and You are more Knowing of his inner self. O Allah, if he was a good-doer, increase in his goodness, and if he was a bad-doer, overlook his sins.
Then you say Takbeer for the second time, and do that in every Takbeer.

key_terms.الْمُسَجَّى: The enshrouded one (wrapped in burial shroud)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific supplications and Takbeer sequence for the prayer over the deceased in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the ritual structure of Salat al-Mayyit, specifically highlighting the theological balance between hope and fear through the supplication 'If he was a doer of good, increase his good; if he was a doer of evil, overlook his evil.' It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on intercessory prayer (Du'a) and the divine attribute of mercy, where the living advocate for the deceased while acknowledging God's ultimate knowledge of the unseen (Sirr).
